findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. User data is readable from the instance metadata service by any process on the host or via SSRF, and is stored unencrypted in the EC2 API and Terraform state, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.

The instance is launched into aws_subnet.web_subnet, which has map_public_ip_on_launch = true and a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, and is attached to a security group open to the world on SSH and HTTP. The host holding the hard-coded credentials is therefore directly reachable from the internet.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available. On an internet-facing web server this makes theft of instance metadata (and any role credentials or the user-data secrets) via SSRF trivial.
No root_block_device encryption is configured, so unless account-level EBS default encryption is enabled the instance root volume is created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
The ingress rule permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative SSH access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the instance.

findings.issue_category: unrestricted egress and cleartext HTTP ingress
findings.description: Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted outbound data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host, while ingress on port 80 from anywhere serves traffic in cleartext with no HTTPS listener defined.
The volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data written to the volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted.

The snapshot is derived from the unencrypted aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage and therefore inherits its unencrypted state, leaving a persistent, shareable copy of the volume data without encryption at rest.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry useful for reconnaissance is stored without an explicitly enforced encryption setting.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block and TLS policy
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, restrictive ACL, or bucket policy requiring aws:SecureTransport is defined, leaving the flow log bucket reliant on account defaults and open to accidental public exposure and cleartext access.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the route table's 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway means every instance launched into this subnet is automatically internet-reachable, removing the network boundary in front of workloads.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the route table carrying a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway mean any instance launched here receives a routable public IP by default.

force_destroy = true allows the flow log bucket and all stored network audit records to be deleted in a single terraform destroy without object-level safeguards, undermining the integrity and availability of security telemetry.
